body: Maximum peak-to-trough fall inside each winner's own up-move (weekly closes), 27 windows: median −41%; 22 of 27 (81%) had at least one ≥30% drawdown, and 14 (52%) at least one ≥40%. Examples: Bajaj Finance −61% (2020), Tata Elxsi −59% (2018–20), APL Apollo −57% (2018–19), BSE −55% (2022–23), Dixon −52% (2021–23), Page −52% (2018–20), Avanti −51% (2012–13), Balkrishna −48%, HAL −47% (2020), Caplin −47% (2013), Polycab −45%, CDSL −44%. The shallowest were Pidilite (−26%), Eicher 2008–17 (−26%), Trent 2020–24 (−22%) and Kaynes (−20%, a short run). Most of these drawdowns came from market shocks (2013 taper, 2018 small-cap crash, 2020 COVID) or de-rating while EPS kept rising (Caplin 2017–20: EPS 2x, price −68%), not from broken theses. Holding rule: a ≥40% fall is the normal cost of a multibagger. The question at −40% is whether EPS and ROCE are intact (hold or add) or the driver has broken (exit). Position size so a −60% move is survivable. Extends insight:winners-drawdowns to India.
title: Median in-run drawdown of Indian multibaggers −41%; 22 of 27 fell ≥30% on the way up

body: RULE: our disqualifier (pledge >25% of promoter holding or rising) stays the DEFAULT; an override must be written down as a decision record. Grade severity on six questions: (1) PURPOSE: disclosed and specific (family debt from a known investment, funding the listed company's own rights issue) vs undisclosed or to fund other group companies; (2) SIZE: % of promoter holding and % of total equity, plus the price cushion before margin calls; (3) TREND: falling via actual stake sales or repayments (Apollo Hospitals: ~76% in 2019 -> ~2% by Aug 2025 after block sales) vs rising while price rises (Zee/Essel 59% -> ~90%); (4) LENDER: banks with long tenor vs NBFCs/MFs with loan-against-shares and short tenor (2018-19 IL&FS freeze turned MF pledges into fire sales); (5) LISTED-COMPANY LEVERAGE: is the company itself unlevered and cash-generative, or does it also guarantee group debt; (6) GROUP HISTORY: any past invocations, diversion or contagion (ADAG, Essel, Future, Cox & Kings = severe). A pledge that is high but falling, disclosed, bank-funded, at the family level, in a clean group with an unlevered company is a sizing and monitoring issue; a rising pledge with undisclosed purpose in a group with a history is a disqualifier. Also treat non-disposal undertakings and 'encumbrances' as pledges. HONEST CAVEAT: even benign pledges are reflexive in a crash; Apollo worked partly because the price rose. Size such positions small and track quarterly SAST disclosures.

data.override_needs: all six checks pass + decision record + small size

title: Grading a promoter pledge: purpose, size, trend, lender, leverage, group history
